summary: This continuation adds configuration-space cohomology and rational double-loop calculations, together with a single semialgebraic C₂-equivariant topology interface for real varieties and ramified covers. It merges all three accepted extraction tranches without replanning ordinary AlgebraicTopology. Every target is assigned a dependency, supplier request or explicit proof obligation; the planning pass is complete, with 15 recorded gaps and no claim that the resulting theory is implemented or closed.

nodes.title: Ordered and unordered configurations
nodes.statement: For a space X and m≥0, PConf_m(X) is the subspace of injective maps Fin m→X; Conf_m(X) is its orbit quotient for (σ·x)(i)=x(σ⁻¹i). For A¹ over ℤ, use the open locus where every x_i−x_j is invertible, and the unordered locus of monic degree-m polynomials with invertible discriminant.
hypotheses: m is a natural number; the topological construction is over a specified space X.
The scheme-valued construction uses unit differences over every test ring.
proofSteps: Form the finite intersection of diagonal complements and the permutation action.
Construct the algebraic discriminant open through symmetric functions; distinguish its ring-valued points from the set-theoretic configuration functor.
acceptance: Over fields the points are ordered distinct tuples; over general rings the differences are units.

nodes.title: Split arrangement purity
nodes.statement: Let A be a finite arrangement of affine hyperplanes defined over F_q and split over F_q. For ℓ≠char F_q, H^a((A^m\⋃A)_Fqbar,Q_ℓ) is generated by logarithmic degree-one classes, vanishes for a>m, and geometric Frobenius acts as q^a. For PConf_m(A¹), m≥1, H_c^a vanishes outside m+1≤a≤2m. For m=0 only a=0 survives.
hypotheses: The arrangement is split over F_q and ℓ is invertible in F_q.
The configuration support assertion separates m=0 from m≥1.
proofSteps: Use deletion–restriction and residue maps to generate arrangement cohomology in degree one.
The dlog classes are Q_ℓ(−1); products give Frobenius q^a. For configurations split off translation A¹ and use the dimension m−1 normalized complement, then duality.
acceptance: The compact-support range differs from the ordinary range; m=1 has H_c² only.

nodes.title: Root Frobenius and full cycle type
nodes.statement: For a squarefree monic polynomial f of degree m over F_q, the Frobenius permutation of its geometric roots has one cycle of length deg P for each irreducible factor P. Its full cycle count is the number of factors, including linear factors; in Mathlib it is card(σ.cycleType)+card(fixedPoints σ).
proofSteps: Identify roots of an irreducible degree-r factor with one Frobenius orbit of size r.
Sum these orbits over the distinct factors; add fixed points omitted by the pinned cycleType convention.
acceptance: Identity on m points has m cycles; (ab)(c) has two; degree-zero polynomial has zero.

nodes.title: Twisted configuration trace formula
nodes.statement: For a finite-dimensional characteristic-zero S_m representation T with character χ, ∑_{f monic squarefree,deg f=m}χ(Frob_f)=∑_a(−1)^a q^{m−a}⟨χ,H^a(PConf_m(ℂ),Q)⟩=∑_i(−1)^{m−i}q^i⟨χ,H_c^{m+i}(PConf_m(ℂ),Q)⟩. All arithmetic-to-Betti comparisons respect the finite-cover local system.
proofSteps: Descend the ordered torsor representation to the unordered finite-field configuration local system.
Apply the compact trace formula and finite-cover descent; use purity and Poincaré duality to obtain the ordinary formula.
Reindex compact degree a=m+i only after duality.

nodes.title: Signed Witt–Euler exponents
nodes.statement: For n,N≥0 define the unique integers e_r(n,N), r≥1, by ∏_{r≥1}(1−T^r)^{−e_r}=1+(−1)^{n−1}NT, where the sign means −1 when n is even and +1 when n is odd. Infinite products are coefficientwise T-adically finite.
proofSteps: Recursively cancel the coefficient of T^r with the rth factor; its linear coefficient changes by e_r.
Prove uniqueness by the first differing coefficient, integrality by recursion, and agreement under truncation.
acceptance: Never define an integer sequence by a rational quotient without proving divisibility.

hypotheses: n≥4 and j,d,N≥0.
proofSteps: Take the weighted diagonal i=m(n−2)−j of the bivariate identity.
The support lower bound excludes m(n−3)>j; hence truncating at d does not change the coefficient.

nodes.title: Tame complex polynomial
nodes.statement: A complex polynomial f:ℂ^n→ℂ is tame if there are a compact neighbourhood K of its critical locus and ε>0 with ‖∇f(z)‖≥ε outside K. If its degree k≥2 leading homogeneous part cuts out a smooth projective hypersurface, then for sufficiently large ‖z‖ one has ‖∇f(z)‖≥c‖z‖^{k−1} for some c>0, so f is tame.
proofSteps: Take the positive minimum of the norm of the leading gradient on the unit sphere, using Euler’s homogeneous identity and projective smoothness.
Bound the lower-degree gradient terms uniformly and absorb them for large radius.
acceptance: A nonzero linear polynomial is handled separately, with constant nonzero gradient.

nodes.title: Tame fibre bouquet theorem
nodes.statement: For tame f:ℂ^n→ℂ, n≥2, and a regular value a, the fibre f⁻¹(a) has the homotopy type of a finite wedge of N spheres S^{n−1}, with N the total sum of local Milnor numbers of f. A nonconstant linear f gives N=0.

Use connectivity, cellular homology and Whitehead to obtain the wedge equivalence; the analytic and Milnor-theoretic inputs are tracked in G1.

nodes.title: Rational homotopy of spheres
nodes.statement: For s≥2 and i≥2, π_i(S^s)⊗Q is Q for i=s, additionally Q for i=2s−1 when s is even, and zero otherwise.

For even s use the unit-tangent sphere fibration and its rational odd-sphere homology to leave the extra degree 2s−1.
Finite generation changes the torsion conclusions to the stated rational ranks; the general Serre spectral sequence is G2.
acceptance: S² has ranks one in degrees 2 and 3; S³ has rank one only in degree 3.

nodes.title: Finite-type rational double-loop model
nodes.statement: If X is simply connected of finite rational type and Ω²X is connected, then the rational cohomology of Ω²X is the free graded-commutative algebra on ⊕_{i≥1}(π_{i+2}(X)⊗Q)^∨ placed in degree i, provided the loop spaces have nilpotent finite-type CW models.

Ω²X is connected and both loop spaces admit nilpotent finite-type CW models.
proofSteps: Use the rational minimal model theorem identifying indecomposables with dual rational homotopy.
The loop model on desuspended generators has zero differential; apply it twice in the connected nilpotent finite-type range.
Record existence and correctness of the minimal-model machinery as G3, rather than replacing it by the asserted cohomology formula.
acceptance: The generator space is dual; connectivity of Ω²X is a hypothesis.

nodes.title: Finite joins and sphere bouquets
nodes.statement: For n≥2 and nonempty finite discrete sets A_1,…,A_n with cardinalities k_i, their topological join has the homotopy type of ∨_{∏(k_i−1)}S^{n−1}; consequently it is (n−2)-connected. A singleton factor makes it contractible. Empty factors are outside this statement.

Induct on the number of colours: collapse one cone and use the cofibration quotient to get a wedge of k_n−1 suspensions of the previous join.
Use Whitehead and cellular homology, including n=2 where the join is a connected complete bipartite graph.
acceptance: For two two-point sets the join is S¹; three give S²; a singleton factor is contractible.

nodes.title: Semialgebraic real and complex loci

nodes.title: Orientation formula and finite duality
nodes.statement: For a semialgebraic map f between homology manifolds of dimensions v,w and F∈D^b(W,Λ) with locally constant cohomology, f!F≅(or_{V/W}⊗f*F)[v−w]. For a locally constant sheaf A of finite abelian groups on V, cup product and trace give a perfect pairing H_c^i(V,A)×H^{v−i}(V,Hom(A,Q/ℤ)⊗or_V)→Q/ℤ. Both adjoint maps are isomorphisms.
hypotheses: The relative formula assumes homology manifolds and bounded locally constant cohomology.
The perfect-pairing assertion assumes finite stalks, not merely bounded exponent.
proofSteps: For the absolute structure map identify its dualizing object with or_V[v] using local chart duality.
Use the adjunction and tensor-Hom compatibility on locally constant bounded objects to deduce the relative formula.
Apply Verdier duality and the injectivity of Q/ℤ; finite stalks and semialgebraic finiteness identify both duals. Derived cup composition agrees with cup product.
acceptance: Finite exponent alone is insufficient: an infinite direct sum of F₂ at a point does not satisfy the algebraic bidual statement.

nodes.title: Semialgebraic finite Borel approximation
nodes.statement: Let G=C₂ act on a semialgebraic V and antipodally on S^s. Descend the pullback of F to F_s on V_s=(V×S^s)/G. For invariant closed Z and Z_s=(Z×S^s)/G, H_G,Z^i(V,F)≅H_{Z_s}^i(V_s,F_s) for i<s, compatibly as s increases. This specializes the SF.2 finite-G Borel carrier; F_s need not be constant.
proofSteps: Use the free quotient to descend the pulled-back sheaf.
The sphere’s reduced cohomology vanishes below s, giving the stable comparison through the relative spectral sequence.
Keep descent and orientation data when applying manifold duality to V_s.
acceptance: For V=pt, V_s=RP^s; stability is claimed strictly below s, and a sign module descends to the nonconstant rank-one local system.

nodes.title: Equivariant purity and proper Gysin
nodes.statement: Finite Borel approximation gives equivariant purity for closed homology-manifold embeddings and proper Gysin maps with relative orientation. For a proper map of smooth pure-dimensional R-varieties f:Y→X and c=dim X−dim Y, its complex-locus map is H_G^a(Y(C),M(−c))→H_G^{a+2c}(X(C),M), whereas its real-locus map has shift c and relative real orientation.
proofSteps: Apply ordinary semialgebraic purity and Gysin to the finite Borel manifolds and pass to their stable degree range.
Compute the complex relative orientation as ℤ(c) and solve the coefficient twist for the stated target.
Prove compatibility with restriction, supports, cup products and proper base change within this topological setting.
acceptance: pt→P¹ has complex degree shift two and real degree shift one; do not use the same shift.

nodes.title: Real-locus self-intersection class
nodes.statement: For smooth pure-d X/R and i:X(R)↪X(C), let s=i_*(1)∈H_G,X(R)^d(X(C),F₂). Define γ_X=(γ_0,…,γ_d)∈⊕_{p=0}^dH^p(X(R),F₂) as the coordinates of i*s after forgetting supports. Then γ_0=1 and γ_X is invertible in total ordinary cohomology; extend its inverse by zero beyond the finite cohomological dimension.

Evaluate at every real point to compute its zeroth coordinate as the local normal fundamental class.
The positive-degree ideal is nilpotent, so the finite geometric series gives a canonical inverse.

nodes.title: Canonical mod-two support splitting

nodes.title: Equivariant Ehresmann transport
nodes.statement: For a proper smooth submersion of finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifolds without boundary f:M→B with involutions commuting with f, near a fixed base point b there is a C₂-equivariant local trivialization over a small invariant neighbourhood, relative to the induced base involution. If the base involution is trivial on the chosen real parameter neighbourhood, the fibre diffeomorphisms commute with the involution. This assertion alone does not transport an arbitrary divisor as a pair.
hypotheses: Source and base are finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifolds without boundary; involutions and f are smooth.
The map f is a proper surjective submersion over the chosen neighbourhood, and b is fixed by the base involution.
proofSteps: Retain the promised ordinary Ehresmann owner MappingClassGroupsAndCanonicalRepresentations (G12). For the horizontal-flow ingredients reuse current DifferentialGeometry Layer 3 and the native Tau Ceti maximalIntegralCurve/maximalIntegralCurveFlowDomain interfaces; GT.1 supplies the manifold carrier, not a second flow theory.

Average a Riemannian metric over the involution on source and base. Linearize the base involution in a small invariant metric exponential ball at b, then lift radial paths using the invariant orthogonal horizontal distribution.
Properness supplies complete lifts on that small neighbourhood. Ordinary theorem ownership and the equivariant extension proof are G12.
acceptance: A product with a nontrivial fibre involution gives the product trivialization; no divisor preservation follows.

nodes.title: Equivariant stratified pair transport
nodes.statement: Let f:M→B be proper on a closed Whitney-stratified subset A⊂M, with every stratum mapping submersively to B, an involution preserving all strata and commuting with f, and chosen invariant f-compatible control data. Locally at a fixed b, controlled horizontal lifts give an equivariant homeomorphic trivialization of A preserving every distinguished union of strata. Apply this to a divisor pair only after verifying these hypotheses for that family.
hypotheses: M and B are finite-dimensional smooth manifolds without boundary, the stratification of the closed subset A is locally finite and Whitney, and the involutions on M and B are smooth with f equivariant; each stratum restriction of f is smooth.
The Whitney strata and distinguished unions are invariant.
The stratified map is proper and stratumwise submersive.
Invariant f-compatible control data are given, not assumed automatically.
proofSteps: Mather’s compatible control data reduce the isotopy lemma to controlled vector fields.
With invariant control data, average controlled lifts (their defining compatibility conditions are linear) and integrate with the properness bounds.
Preservation of each stratum gives a homeomorphism of every named pair. Existence of invariant control data and application to Benoist’s divisor are G13.
acceptance: A family with a changing divisor crossing fails stratified submersivity and is not covered. This does not silently upgrade ordinary Ehresmann.

nodes.title: Finite-index equivariant lattice image
nodes.statement: For a compact finite-CW-type G-space T and a finitely generated coefficient system ℤ(j), the forgetful image H_G²(T,ℤ(j))→H²(T,ℤ(j))^G has finite index. Rationally it is an isomorphism onto invariants.
proofSteps: Use the Hochschild–Serre edge map; all outgoing obstruction groups from bidegree (0,2) are finite because positive C₂ cohomology is killed by two and the ordinary groups are finitely generated.
Rational averaging kills every positive-group-degree term, giving full rational span; a full-rank subgroup of a finitely generated abelian group has finite index.
acceptance: Finite index is not integral surjectivity; the proof allows nonzero 2-primary obstructions.

nodes.title: Double-cover chase comparison
nodes.statement: For the ramified-cover triangle represented by a short exact sequence of bounded-below injective equivariant complexes, tensor with 0→ℤ→ℤ[G]→ℤ(1)→0 and take equivariant sections. Let γ∈H³(T₀(C),ℤ), let δ∈H_G³(S₀(C),ℤ) have ordinary image Tr(γ), and let ζ∈H_G³(S*(C),L(1)) satisfy κ(ζ)=N(γ)∈H_G³(T₀(C),ℤ(1)), where N is the regular-coefficient norm and κ is the twisted triangle map. For g:H_G³(S₀(C),ℤ)→H_G⁴(S*(C),L) the triangle boundary, there exists η₀∈H_G²(S₀(C),ℤ(1)) with g(δ)+ζ∪ω=g(η₀∪ω). The existence statement is modulo the displayed image; η₀ is not a canonical choice.
proofSteps: Replace the triangle by injective complexes and justify injectivity after tensoring with the three finite free coefficient modules (their tensor functors have exact adjoints).
The resulting 3×3 short-exact double diagram produces the two chases and their indeterminacy.

Verify that the displayed two lifts of the common γ give precisely the plus sign and the displayed indeterminacy, using a cochain chase in the 3×3 diagram or Jannsen’s lemma; this proof obligation is G14.
acceptance: Both chased terms must have coefficient L in degree four; the conclusion is modulo the image g(−∪ω), not literal equality of arbitrarily chosen chases.
